40.name: Sujata Dash

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sujata Dash is a poet from Bhubaneswar and a retired banker. Her work appears regularly in literary journals and anthologies. A 2025 contributor note in Our Poetry Archive lists four poetry collections with Authorspress: “More than Mere”, “Riot of Hues”, “Eternal Rhythm” and “Humming Serenades”. Her Kabita Live biography also records her studies in English literature and her writing in Odia, Hindi and English.

The poems here bring natural imagery into difficult emotional weather. “Twigs of Hope” seeks a small, persistent resource amid grief; “I Grieve My Loss” moves from mechanical days towards air, mist and dawn. “It Is Not to Be” adds moral unease to that struggle, questioning material comfort at the expense of human bonds. “Offbeat” offers a lighter counterpoint, with a speaker determined to keep an individual rhythm rather than organise life by other people’s timetables.

106.name: Mandakini Bhattacharjee

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Mandakini Bhattacharjee is a multilingual poet, critic and translator associated with Kolkata. Publishing as Mandakini Bhattacherya, she teaches English at Fakir Chand College, Diamond Harbour. Her work includes editing The Mixed Fare, a short-story anthology, and co-translating Jatin Bala’s A Life Uprooted: A Bengali Dalit Refugee Remembers with Jaydeep Sarangi, published by Sahitya Akademi in 2022.

Her poems in Kabita Live turn small physical things into measures of intimacy and memory. In ‘The Unkindest Cut’, the changing life of a wound becomes a way of thinking about love and forgetting. In ‘Pearldom’, a broken necklace moves from an ornament against the skin to scattered beads gathered and kept: the object holds what the lovers remember.

142.name: Nisith Raj

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: A literary critic and author, Raj has worked across editorial practice and support for fellow writers through Literia Insight and The Literary Mirror. paragraphs: Soumen Ray’s contributor biography identifies him as Soumen Roy, the author of the novel Scar and the poetry collection Lyrical Musings. Both titles were reviewed by Literoma in January 2023. Bookseller catalogues list Lyrical Musings under the Roy spelling, with a 2022 Notion Press edition.

192.name: Neelam Saxena Chandra

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Neelam Saxena Chandra writes poetry, fiction and children’s stories in Hindi and English. An engineering graduate whose professional background includes Indian Railways, she has developed a literary practice across both languages. Her poetry catalogue includes The Stitched Heart and एक क़दम रौशनी की ओर, collections that reflect her recurring interest in inner strength and renewal.

Her Kabita Live poem ‘Happiness’ follows the changing meanings of pleasure from childhood curiosity through adult ambition to a later awareness of impermanence. In ‘क्या नज़्म लिखूँ तुमपर?’, praise continually exceeds what words can hold: birdsong, moonlight and a river become ways of addressing someone whose presence already seems to be a poem.

195.name: Tandra Mishra

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Tandra Mishra writes poetry in English and Bengali. A contributor biography in Literary Vibes places her in Raiganj, West Bengal, records her postgraduate study of English and identifies Oh Father! as her first poetry collection. Her writing brings questions of women's freedom and dignity into a wider concern with social life.

In her Kabita Live poem I am a Girl, the repeated declaration of identity gathers strength through a succession of roles: worker, artist, soldier, caregiver and creator. Public achievement sits beside the less acknowledged labour of sustaining a home. The poem's direct address asks that care and courage be recognised together, rather than treating tenderness as the opposite of power.

218.name: Zakir Khan / ଜାକିର ଖାନ

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Zakir Khan writes Odia poetry and fiction alongside work in journalism and translation. His contributions to Samata and Sahitya Charcha establish that literary range, while an Odisha government library-selection record lists his Nandan Kaanan, published by Pakshighara Prakashanee. His writing here often asks how language can respond to the pressures of social and economic life.

Eka Arthanaitika Kabita, dedicated to Kishan Pattnayak, asks whether a poem can serve ordinary people, farmers and forest communities. Gote Gapara Plot turns a father's ambition for his son into a painful story of material success and solitude. Elsewhere, Manisha imagines an overturned natural world to question territorial division, Bata makes the road itself a philosophical companion, and Kabitatiera Apekhare waits for poetry to return to a blank sheet carried in a pocket.

255.name: Tulika

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Tulika writes Hindi poetry and works across communication teaching and documentary film. An Amity University faculty profile records her co-direction of “Khanabadosh” and recognition for the poetry manuscript “Gulabi Canvas”. These parallel practices bring words and images into her work, while her poem here speaks directly to the contradictions surrounding women’s education and independence.

“Beti Bachao Beti Padhao” tests a familiar public slogan against the treatment of daughters who actually grow, study and make choices. Its recurring phrase becomes an accumulating indictment: achievement is praised in principle, yet resistance to violence, independent movement and single motherhood attract suspicion. The closing turn from being cherished to fighting for affection exposes the distance between public approval and the freedom a woman is allowed at home.

318.name: Ranu Uniyal

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Ranu Uniyal writes poetry in English and Hindi and teaches English at the University of Lucknow. She completed her doctorate at the University of Hull; her academic interests include women’s writing, disability studies and poetry. Her collections include Across the Divide, December Poems, The Day We Went Strawberry Picking in Scarborough and Saeeda Ke Ghar.

Her Kabita Live poems bring landscape close to the senses while questioning how people inhabit it. “Plums versus Pullum” begins with the taste and local name of fruit, recalling Ranikhet, Almora and a mother’s kitchen. “At Kedarnath” turns to the force of a flood, using the imagery of Shiva and a river’s voice to challenge human disregard for the natural world.

paragraphs: Reema Sinha is a Lucknow writer and the founder of Niharika Sahitya Manch, a forum for literary and cultural gatherings. Her contributions to Kabita Live appear in Hindi and English, bringing together devotional address and attentiveness to another person’s feelings.

In “भक्तिन के नयनों में अमर प्रेम रहने दो”, flowers, sandalwood and prayer frame love as a sustained act of devotion. “That old woman” turns instead to an encounter in moonlight: the observer senses grief and remembered joy but cannot fully understand them. Both poems approach feeling through what can be seen, offered or left unsaid.

366.name: Neha Bhandarkar

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Neha Bhandarkar is a poet, author and translator who writes in Marathi, Hindi and English. Her contributor biography in Our Poetry Archive identifies her with Nagpur and describes her work as a Marathi newspaper columnist. The Guntur International Poetry Festival lists her book Hues of Fusion among its festival releases.

In her Kabita Live poem ‘Worthy Meeting’, an encounter becomes an exchange of gifts with the natural world. Clouds, rain, sunlight and a rainbow take on the qualities of clothing, music and adornment. The poem gathers these changing seasons into a wish to return, making the meeting both intimate and expansive.

382.name: Gopikrishnan Kottoor

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Gopikrishnan Kottoor is an Indian poet whose work also includes drama, translation and literary editing. He founded the poetry journal Poetry Chain and edited A New Book of Poems in English. His contributor note in Shot Glass Journal records appearances in Best Asian Poetry, Acumen and Nth Position.

His collection A Land in the Sun, published by Penprints, offers an entry into a body of work concerned with love, loss, nature and ordinary experience. The publisher highlights poems such as ‘My Father’s Shirt’ and ‘The Last Man in the Bar’. These are starting points in his wider published work; the current Kabita Live catalogue does not yet link a poem to this profile.

404.name: Pallabi Das

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Pallabi Das writes in Odia and English. Her connection with the literary life of Junagarh, Kalahandi, is reflected in local reporting on poetry gatherings, including the inauguration of the town’s Sahitya Sanskruti Sansad in February 2024.

In ‘Beauty with Brain’, an affectionate address to a mother opens outward into the excitement of lunar exploration. The names Bikram and Pragyan bring technological achievement into a language of love and admiration. The poem joins wonder at the moon with gratitude toward the figure it addresses.

408.name: Padmashree R.P.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Padmashree R.P. is a Bengaluru poet and teacher trainer. Her public writing brings poetry into conversation with education, while her contribution here attends to the ways affection and knowledge pass between generations.

‘Love’s Simplicity’ moves between the body, family memory and the natural world. Rivers, blood, parents’ songs and children form a chain of shared experience. Its recurring short passages give the poem a gentle, reflective rhythm, presenting love as something learned through attention and companionship.

410.name: Rima Sinha

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Rima Sinha writes poetry in Hindi. Her Kabita Live contribution carries a Lucknow byline; Sahitya Rachana has also published Hindi poetry under the name रीमा सिन्हा, identifying the writer with Lucknow.

In “रख लिया विक्षोभ बहुत”, the speaker turns from inner unrest towards devotion. The contrast between an assertion of rights and Radha’s love opens a sequence of promises: to understand the beloved, share the road and offer shade against life’s heat. Repetition gives these promises the cadence of a personal vow.

423.name: Youngbo Ma

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Youngbo Ma's contributor note describes a poet from mainland China who writes in Chinese and English and translates between the two languages. Almost a Kind of Responsibility introduces that work through a sustained meditation on what it means to begin a poem.

Writing becomes a form of carpentry: the hands search among tools, words produce shavings, and every new attempt requires skills to be learned afresh. Yet the poem questions whether technique can guarantee anything, or whether unnoticed labour can lessen suffering. Its quiet ending returns to the ordinary fact of sunlight and existence. The responsibility lies in beginning again, even without certainty that the work will matter.

429.name: Bharati Hazarika

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Bharati Hazarika is a multilingual writer from Guwahati. Her contributor profile in Gems V records work in poetry, stories and articles; the anthology includes her poems on the natural world and human equality. Kabita Live’s contributor note also describes her writing for children and her work with lyrics and music.

Her Kabita Live poems bring public concerns into direct, insistent language. “Freedom Is Our Birthright” answers physical restraint with the freedom of thought and spirit, returning to its declaration like a refrain. “Glacier” turns from the beauty of ice and its living surroundings towards an urgent appeal to care for the earth. Together, the poems move between human dignity and responsibility towards the natural world.

438.name: Zahir Hossain Baidya

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Zahir Hossain Baidya's poetry is rooted in the intensity of feeling and the effort to give it a written form. His contribution to Fakir Chand College's 2022–23 magazine, The Lone-Wolf, identifies him as an English Honours student. That dated publication provides an early point of reference for the questioning, emotionally charged voice encountered in his work here.

Sinister Sense begins with a reported proposal about stray dogs, then turns its attention to the human threat faced by women in public places. Its harsh, deliberately disturbing questions give way to an appeal for protection. The poem's animal and floral imagery makes a pointed contrast between predation and vulnerable life; the speaker's anger is part of its rhetoric, rather than a biographical account of the poet.

449.name: Tulika Bibidh Rang / तूलिका विविध रंग

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Tulika Bibidh Rang writes Hindi poetry alongside work in communication education. Amity University’s faculty profile identifies her with its School of Communication in Madhya Pradesh and records interests in traditional media, audiovisual storytelling and folk art. The same profile records a 2021 Pen In Books Young Author Award for her Hindi poetry manuscript “Gulabi Canvas”.

In “Basanti Budget”, the language of examinations, meetings, growth and financial planning is redirected towards emotional life. Against an exhausting race for achievement, the poem proposes making room for family laughter, neighbourly food, affection and hope. Spring becomes a model of change that is generous rather than merely competitive; the budget worth balancing is one that leaves space for shared happiness.
